docs.title: AAuth Postman Collections
docs.text: Postman collections for AAuth (draft-hardt-oauth-aauth-protocol-11): every access mode as a folder of requests you can send, from agent identity to federated authorization, with values passed from each response to the next request and checks on every response.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
• Generated, not hand-written. The collections are generated by PIDL from the AAuth protocol document in agent-protocols, the same document behind its AAuth Explorer, so the requests, order and checks match the walkthrough step for step.
  • Postman plays the agent. The agent provider, resource, person server and access server are real servers: the AAuth sandbox from aauth-go runs them all, on a laptop, in Docker or on Kubernetes.
  • Signing happens outside Postman. Every AAuth request carries an HTTP message signature (RFC 9421). Requests go through the sandbox's signing helper, which signs them with the agent's key and forwards them.

docs.title: What Is Included
docs.text:
Collection Environment What it runs aauth sandbox The five access modes against the sandbox's demo resources: 21 requests, 98 assertions petstore petstore Browsing the Petstore and placing an order that needs the person's approval: 10 requests, 47 assertions aauth-mock mock The walkthrough's example responses, for a Postman mock server

The files are in collections/ and environments/.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
With Docker and an aauth-go checkout at ../../aauth-dev/aauth-go:

docker compose up -d --build --wait             # the sandbox: every role and the signing helper
docker compose --profile test run --rm newman   # run every access mode with Newman

In Postman, import collections/aauth.postman_collection.json and environments/sandbox.postman_environment.json, select the environment, and run a folder. Postman talks only to the signing helper at http://127.0.0.1:8099, so no hosts entries or certificates are needed.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
• Running Against the Sandbox: Docker or a local sandbox, how signing works, mock mode, and regenerating the collections.

  • Interop Testing: a runbook, for people and AI agents, for testing an agent, resource or server of your own against the sandbox.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:

  • agent-protocols: the AAuth protocol document and the AAuth Explorer.

docs.title: Interop Testing
docs.text: A runbook for checking that an AAuth agent, resource or person server works against the others, for people and for AI agents running the steps for them. The servers come from the AAuth sandbox in aauth-go; its sandbox guide is the reference for every option used here.

docs.title: Pick What You Are Testing
docs.text:
You are testing Start the sandbox with Then An agent (a client of your own) the Compose file in this repository enroll at https://ap.aauth.test/enroll, call the Petstore or https://resource.aauth.test A resource (a server of your own) --upstream name=http://your-server, see Front your own server run the collection or an agent against https://name.aauth.test A person server, agent provider or access server --remote ps=https://your-server, see Test another implementation run the collection; the sandbox's other roles call yours

The two reference agents are this repository's Postman collections (one request per step, so you can read each message) and omniagent (an AI agent that signs requests itself; see its AAuth guide).

docs.title: Run the Reference Setup
docs.text:
docker compose up -d --build --wait                          # part 1: the sandbox
docker compose --profile test run --rm newman                # 21 requests, 98 assertions
docker compose --profile petstore up -d --build --wait       # part 2: adds the Petstore
docker compose --profile petstore run --rm newman-petstore   # 10 requests, 47 assertions

Part 1 needs only an aauth-go checkout. Part 2 also needs a petstore checkout; skip it to test with the sandbox's own resources.

A passing run reports 0 failed. This is the baseline: if it fails, fix the setup before testing anything of your own.

Two checks that the baseline is healthy:

docker compose --profile petstore ps                                 # sandbox and petstore: healthy
docker compose exec sandbox aauth-sandbox trace --state /state | head # the message trace

docs.title: Test an Agent of Your Own
docs.text:
Inside the Compose network, the roles answer at their names, so an agent container needs no hosts entries. Run it on the same network and trust the sandbox CA from the shared state volume (/state/ca.pem):

  1. Enroll at the agent provider: POST https://ap.aauth.test/enroll with your public key. The response is an agent token.
  2. Call https://petstore.aauth.test/v2/pet/findByStatus?status=available, signed (RFC 9421) with Signature-Key carrying the agent token. Expect 200.
  3. Call POST https://petstore.aauth.test/v2/store/order. Expect 401 with AAuth-Requirement: requirement=person-token, then, after you obtain a person token, 401 with requirement=auth-token and a resource token.
  4. Send the resource token to https://ps.aauth.test/token. Expect 202 with a Location and an interaction code while the person approves, then 200 with the auth token. The sandbox approves on its own unless started with --consent manual.
  5. Repeat the order with the auth token. Expect 200.

The trace shows each message, so compare yours with the Postman run, step by step.

docs.title: Test with an AI Agent
docs.text:
omniagent is a ready-made agent for this:

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... docker compose --profile omniagent run --rm -T omniagent \
  --prompt "Call the place-order tool now with petId 2 and quantity 1. I have already confirmed; do not ask."

Expect Enrolled as aauth:assistant@ap.aauth.test, then Approval needed. Open … and the order result. Notes for agents running this:

  • Check pet ids first: GET /v2/pet/findByStatus?status=available. A sold pet is gone until the Petstore restarts; recreate the sandbox with it (docker compose --profile petstore up -d --wait --force-recreate sandbox petstore), see Troubleshooting.
  • The model decides what to call. If it asks for confirmation or searches by a tag that matches nothing, state the tool and arguments, as above. That is the model, not AAuth.
  • Judge success from the trace, not from the model's wording: the order request shows 200 and the person-server /token exchange shows 202 then 200.

docs.title: See a Run in the Walkthrough
docs.text:
make demo (Newman) or make demo-omniagent (omniagent) runs the Petstore order flow and writes demo/live.html, the AAuth walkthrough with the run's messages beside each step. It is the quickest way to compare your agent's messages with the protocol's: recreate the sandbox and the Petstore, run your agent against them, then turn the sandbox's trace into the page:

docker compose --profile petstore up -d --wait --force-recreate sandbox petstore
# ...run your agent...
make demo-page

A step marked "Not seen" is one your run did not perform; an exchange marked "Not a step in the document" is one it made that the protocol does not describe. "Weak match" means only the participants and method agreed. A match means the message looked like the step, not that it was valid.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix bind: address already in use on 8099 or 443 Another program uses the host port SIGNER_PORT=18099 SANDBOX_HTTPS_PORT=18443 docker compose up -d --wait; containers are unaffected connection refused to ap.aauth.test:443 from a container The sandbox listens on loopback only (an overriding command without --listen-any-interface) Use this repository's compose.yaml, or add --listen 0.0.0.0:443 --listen-any-interface 421 Misdirected Request from the signing helper The helper answers only loopback names Add --signer-host <service-name> for the name your client uses x509: certificate signed by unknown authority The client does not trust the sandbox CA Point it at /state/ca.pem, or export it with aauth-sandbox ca export Order fails after a previous run The pet was sold Recreate the sandbox and the Petstore together: docker compose --profile petstore up -d --wait --force-recreate sandbox petstore invalid_resource_token ("no key … in JWKS of https://petstore.aauth.test") after restarting the Petstore The Petstore creates a new signing key at each start, and the person server keeps the key it saw Recreate the sandbox together with the Petstore, as above Old CA after rebuilding The state volume held a CA from an older sandbox docker compose down -v, then start again, and trust the new CA

docs.title: Clean Up
docs.text: docker compose down -v      # removes the containers and the sandbox's keys

docs.title: The Petstore Demos
docs.text: The Swagger Petstore runs next to the sandbox as an AAuth resource at https://petstore.aauth.test. Browsing needs only the agent's identity; placing an order needs the person's approval for write:orders. It is the second part of the setup, so the sandbox can be run and studied without it.

docs.title: Start It
docs.text:
With Docker, an aauth-go checkout at ../../aauth-dev/aauth-go and a petstore checkout (v0.2.0 or later) at ../../grokify/petstore:

docker compose --profile petstore up -d --build --wait      # the sandbox and the Petstore
docker compose --profile petstore run --rm newman-petstore  # the Petstore collection

Set AAUTH_GO_DIR or PETSTORE_DIR if a checkout is elsewhere.

To start over, or to make the pets available to order again, recreate the sandbox and the Petstore together:

docker compose --profile petstore up -d --wait --force-recreate sandbox petstore

The Petstore creates a new signing key each time it starts, and the sandbox's person server keeps the key it saw.

docs.title: Two Agents, the Same Messages
docs.text:
Two demos play the agent against the same servers, so they send the same messages:

Demo The agent Run it Postman Postman, one step per request collections/petstore.postman_collection.json with environments/petstore.postman_environment.json, or docker compose --profile petstore run --rm newman-petstore omniagent omniagent, an AI agent whose tools are the Petstore's operations ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... docker compose --profile petstore run --rm omniagent

In the Postman folder each challenge is a request you can inspect:

  1. The order is refused with 401 and AAuth-Requirement: requirement=person-token.
  2. With a person token, it is refused again with requirement=auth-token and a resource token.
  3. The person server asks the person to approve; the sandbox approves on its own.
  4. The order goes through with the auth token.

omniagent does the same steps inside its HTTP client and prints the approval link. It needs an omniagent checkout at ../../plexusone/omniagent (or OMNIAGENT_DIR) until its image is published. Compare the two in the sandbox's trace:

docker compose exec sandbox aauth-sandbox trace --state /state

docs.title: See Your Run Beside the Protocol
docs.text:
make demo runs the Petstore order flow against fresh servers, captures the sandbox's trace of every message, and writes demo/live.html: the AAuth walkthrough with this run's messages beside each step. Open it in a browser; it needs no server.

make demo             # Newman plays the agent
make demo-omniagent   # omniagent plays the agent; needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or another model's key)

Each scenario the run performed appears as an "Observed" entry after the scenario it is an instance of. A Newman run is found as two: agent identity (browsing) and PS authorization challenged on the API call (the order). Each step shows:

  • the real request and response, with when it happened and the gap from the step before;
  • whether it matched the step strongly, weakly, or not at all, or could not be observed, such as the person approving in a browser;
  • each token, decoded but not verified, with raw values masked;
  • the exchanges the protocol does not describe, such as servers fetching each other's keys, between the steps they fell between.

A Concept / Observed switch shows the document's example instead. The run is matched to the steps by pidl with the binding in bindings/sandbox-petstore.binding.json.

The targets run pidl v0.10.0 with go run and fetch the AAuth document from the agent-protocols v0.9.0 release, so they need Go and network access but no checkouts of either; see Regenerating to use other versions. demo/ holds the raw trace, with real development tokens, and is not committed.

To show a run of your own agent instead, see See a Run in the Walkthrough.

docs.title: Running the Collection Against the Sandbox
docs.text: The signed collection drives the agent side of every AAuth access mode against real servers: the AAuth sandbox from aauth-go runs the agent provider, resource, person server and access server in one process.

docs.title: Quick Start with Docker
docs.text:
docker compose up -d --wait                     # every role plus the signing helper
docker compose --profile test run --rm newman   # run the collection with Newman
docker compose down -v                          # stop and remove the sandbox's keys

Every sandbox option is in the aauth-go sandbox guide; to test an implementation of your own, see the interop runbook.

The sandbox is built from a sibling aauth-go checkout (AAUTH_GO_DIR, default ../../aauth-dev/aauth-go) until its image is published. SIGNER_PORT changes the helper's host port (default 8099), and SANDBOX_HTTPS_PORT the roles' (default 443). Both are published on 127.0.0.1 only.

The Petstore is a second part: add it with docker compose --profile petstore up -d --build --wait and run its collection with docker compose --profile petstore run --rm newman-petstore. See the interop runbook.

Postman needs only the helper: import the collection and the sandbox environment, set signer_url if you changed the port, and run. The steps below are for running the sandbox without Docker, or for talking to the roles directly from a browser.

docs.title: 1. Name the Servers
docs.text:
AAuth server identifiers are https:// origins with a domain name and no port, so each role has its own name under the reserved .test domain. Add them to /etc/hosts:

127.0.0.1  ap.aauth.test ps.aauth.test as.aauth.test resource.aauth.test docs.aauth.test

aauth-sandbox hosts prints this line.

Name Role ap.aauth.test Agent provider ps.aauth.test Person server as.aauth.test Access server resource.aauth.test Resource whose tokens the person server decides docs.aauth.test Resource with its own access server (federated authorization)

docs.title: 2. Start the Sandbox
docs.text:
aauth-sandbox init         # once: creates a local certificate authority and the keys
aauth-sandbox serve        # every role on :443, signing helper on 127.0.0.1:8099

Consent is approved automatically, so runs do not stop for a browser.

docs.title: 3. Trust the Sandbox CA (Direct Access Only)
docs.text:
Requests through the signing helper need no certificate setup. To reach the roles directly, from a browser for example, trust the sandbox's CA:

aauth-sandbox ca export > aauth-sandbox-ca.pem
# or, with Docker:
docker compose exec sandbox aauth-sandbox ca export --state /state > aauth-sandbox-ca.pem

In Postman: Settings > Certificates > CA certificates, and select aauth-sandbox-ca.pem.

docs.title: 4. Run
docs.text:
Import collections/aauth.postman_collection.json and environments/sandbox.postman_environment.json, select the environment, and run a folder. Or from the command line:

npx newman@6 run collections/aauth.postman_collection.json \
  -e environments/sandbox.postman_environment.json

docs.title: How Signing Works
docs.text:
Postman cannot create HTTP message signatures, so every signed request goes to the sandbox's signing helper at {{signer_url}}, followed by the real target URL. The request's Signature-Key header tells the helper how to sign:

Signature-Key Meaning sig=jwt;jwt="{{agent_token}}" Present that token, saved from an earlier response, as the agent, person or auth token its typ names sig=jwt Present the helper's own agent token sig=jkt-jwt Agent provider enrollment sig=hwk Sign with the header web key scheme

The helper replaces it with the real Signature-Key, and adds Content-Digest for bodies and the Signature-Input and Signature headers, using the test agent's keys. Requests that carry no signature are sent directly.

docs.title: Mock Mode
docs.text: collections/aauth-mock.postman_collection.json carries the walkthrough's example responses as saved examples. Create a Postman mock server from it, set mock_url in environments/mock.postman_environment.json, and step through the scenarios without running anything. Mock mode signs nothing and checks only status codes.

docs.title: Regenerating
docs.text:
The collections and environments are generated with pidl from the documents in pidl/ and targets.json:

make generate
Document Collections Scenarios pidl/aauth_sandbox.json aauth, aauth-mock The five access modes, as the sandbox's resources perform them pidl/aauth_petstore.json petstore Browsing the pets and placing an order

Both extend the AAuth document, aauth/pidl/aauth_protocol.json in agent-protocols, which make fetches from a release into pidl/aauth_protocol.json. The sandbox document leaves out the variant in which the resource challenges on the API call, because the sandbox's resources publish an authorization endpoint instead; the Petstore's order flow performs it.

Variable Default Sets PIDL_VERSION v0.10.0 The pidl release that go run uses PIDL go run github.com/grokify/pidl/cmd/pidl@$(PIDL_VERSION) The pidl command, such as PIDL="go -C ../../grokify/pidl run ./cmd/pidl" for a checkout AAUTH_PROTOCOLS_VERSION v0.9.0 The agent-protocols release the AAuth document comes from AAUTH_DOC A local AAuth document to use instead, such as an agent-protocols checkout's CURL curl The curl command that fetches it

docs.title: aauth-postman v0.1.0 Release Notes
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-10-27

The first release: Postman collections for every AAuth access mode, a sandbox to run them against with one command, and a demo that shows a real run beside the protocol. The collections are generated from the same AAuth document as the AAuth Explorer, so what you send in Postman is what the walkthrough explains, step for step.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Every AAuth access mode as a Postman folder, generated by pidl from the AAuth (draft-11) document in agent-protocols
  • One Compose file runs the aauth-go sandbox and, as an optional second part, the Petstore as an AAuth resource, with Newman runs of both collections
  • make demo shows a real run beside the AAuth walkthrough, step by step

docs.title: Collections
docs.text:
Collection Environment What it runs Requests Assertions aauth sandbox Agent identity, resource-managed access (two-party), person identity, PS authorization (three-party) and federated authorization (four-party), against the sandbox's demo resources 21 98 petstore petstore Browsing the pets with the agent's identity, then placing an order that is challenged for a person token, then an auth token 10 47 aauth-mock mock The walkthrough's example responses, for a Postman mock server

Each request passes the values it needs from earlier responses and checks the response it gets.

docs.title: Signing
docs.text: Postman cannot create HTTP message signatures (RFC 9421), so signed requests go to the sandbox's signing helper. The request's Signature-Key header tells the helper what to present: a token saved from an earlier response, identified by its typ; the helper's own agent token; agent provider enrollment; or a header web key. The helper signs the request with the test agent's keys and forwards it. See How Signing Works.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
docker compose up -d --build --wait                          # part 1: the sandbox
docker compose --profile test run --rm newman                # the access modes
docker compose --profile petstore up -d --build --wait       # part 2: adds the Petstore
docker compose --profile petstore run --rm newman-petstore   # the Petstore

The sandbox and the Petstore are built from sibling checkouts of aauth-go and petstore (v0.2.0 or later) until their images are published. SIGNER_PORT and SANDBOX_HTTPS_PORT move the host ports when 8099 or 443 are taken. The omniagent service plays the Petstore's agent with omniagent, an AI agent, instead of Postman.

docs.title: Seeing a Run Beside the Protocol
docs.text: make demo runs the Petstore order flow against fresh servers, captures the sandbox's trace and writes demo/live.html: the AAuth walkthrough with each scenario the run performed added as an "Observed" entry. A Newman run is found as two scenario instances, agent identity and PS authorization challenged on the API call, with every step matched strongly and every token identified by its type. Raw tokens and signatures are masked. make demo-omniagent does the same with omniagent as the agent, and make demo-page writes the page from a run of your own agent. See The Petstore Demos.

docs.title: Generating
docs.text: make generate writes the collections and environments from the documents in pidl/, which extend the AAuth document, and from targets.json. The make targets run pidl v0.10.0 with go run and fetch the AAuth document from the agent-protocols v0.9.0 release, so they need Go and network access but no checkouts. PIDL_VERSION, PIDL, AAUTH_PROTOCOLS_VERSION, AAUTH_DOC and CURL select other versions or local copies; see Regenerating.
